c.tagline: Cuban sandwiches, Gulf sunsets, and Ybor City's neon nights.

taxi.fareNote: Metered street taxis exist but ride-hailing apps (Uber/Lyft) are far more common and usually cheaper for visitors.

emergency.note: 911 is the single nationwide emergency number connecting to police, fire, and ambulance.

english.label: Easy to get by in English

avoid.reason: Caution in some inner neighborhoods; tourist/waterfront zones fine

hood_desc: Tampa's revitalized core along the Riverwalk, anchored by the Water Street district, the Tampa Museum of Art, and Amalie Arena; the most walkable base for first-timers with new luxury hotels and waterfront dining.

The historic Latin Quarter founded by Cuban, Spanish, and Italian cigar workers, now a National Historic Landmark district of red-brick streets, cigar shops, and Tampa's liveliest bar and club scene along 7th Avenue.

A leafy, upscale South Tampa neighborhood of bungalows and oak-lined streets built around Hyde Park Village's boutiques and the SoHo (South Howard) restaurant and bar strip; good for a stylish, residential stay.
A compact waterfront district by the cruise port with the Florida Aquarium, Sparkman Wharf's open-air food hall, and Channelside dining; walkable and connected to downtown by the free streetcar.

Tampa's business and shopping hub near the airport, home to the International Plaza and Bay Street mall and a dense cluster of full-service hotels; convenient for flyers and business travelers though car-dependent.

water.note: Tap water is safe to drink, though some prefer filtered for taste.

transit.hours: HART buses generally run from about 5am to 11pm with reduced weekend service; the streetcar runs roughly 7am to 11pm (later on weekends).
transit.note: Tampa has no metro or rail transit; the heritage TECO streetcar links downtown, Channelside, and Ybor City, while HART buses cover the wider county. A car or ride-hail is often needed beyond the core.
transit.pay: Buy a single HART bus ride ($2) or day pass through the Flamingo Fares app or with cash on board; the TECO Line Streetcar between downtown and Ybor City is fare-free.

transit.m: HART Route 30 bus to downtown (~35 min)
Taxi or rideshare to downtown (15-20 min)

tip.r: ~15-20% at sit-down restaurants is expected; round up or ~15% for taxis and bar service.

food.name: Cuban sandwich
food.desc: Tampa's own version - roast pork, ham, Genoa salami, Swiss, pickle and mustard pressed in Cuban bread. The salami is the local marker.

places.name: Columbia Restaurant
places.note: Florida's oldest restaurant, open since 1905; the benchmark Tampa Cuban in a tiled palace.

places.name: La Segunda Bakery & Cafe
places.note: Baking Tampa's Cuban bread since 1915 and supplying half the city's sandwich shops.

places.name: West Tampa Sandwich Shop
places.note: No-frills counter beloved by locals for a plainly excellent pressed Cuban.

food.name: Deviled crab
food.desc: Croqueta de jaiba - spiced blue crab packed in Cuban-bread dough, breaded and deep fried into a torpedo. Pure Ybor cigar-worker food.

places.name: Brocato's Sandwich Shop
places.note: Family shop that many Tampanians name first for deviled crabs and Cubans alike.

places.name: La Segunda Bakery & Cafe
places.note: Century-old bakery counter selling deviled crabs and empanadas beside the bread ovens.

places.name: Alessi Bakery
places.note: Open since 1912; Sicilian-Tampanian bakery famous for deviled crabs and Cuban sandwiches.

food.name: The original 1905 Salad
food.desc: Iceberg tossed tableside with ham, Swiss, olives, romano and a garlic-Worcestershire vinaigrette - invented in Ybor and copied statewide.

places.name: Columbia Restaurant
places.note: Where the salad was created; still tossed at your table by a waiter with a flourish.

places.name: Columbia Cafe
places.note: The downtown offshoot serving the same salad with a view of the Hillsborough River.

food.name: Grouper sandwich
food.desc: Thick Gulf grouper fillet - blackened, grilled or fried - on a soft bun with lettuce, tomato and tartar. Florida's coastal staple.

places.name: Ulele
places.note: Riverfront restaurant in a restored waterworks building, cooking Florida native ingredients.

places.name: Oystercatchers
places.note: Waterfront seafood room on Old Tampa Bay with a long-standing reputation for Gulf fish.

places.name: Rusty Pelican
places.note: Causeway landmark with sunset views over the bay and reliable grouper.

food.name: Spanish bean soup and boliche
food.desc: Garbanzo soup with chorizo, potato and saffron, and boliche - eye round stuffed with chorizo, braised and sliced over yellow rice.

places.name: La Teresita Restaurant
places.note: Cafeteria-counter institution where Tampa eats Cuban home cooking cheaply and fast.

places.name: Columbia Restaurant
places.note: The formal version of the classics, unchanged for generations.

places.name: Carmine's Restaurant
places.note: Seventh Avenue mainstay for Cuban plates, soups and a famously loaded Cuban sandwich.

food.name: Cuban bread and guava pastelitos
food.desc: Long palm-frond-scored loaves baked daily, plus flaky pastries filled with guava paste and sweet cream cheese.

places.name: La Segunda Central Bakery
places.note: Turns out thousands of loaves a day; the guava-and-cheese pastelitos sell out early.

places.name: Alessi Bakery
places.note: Over a century of Tampa baking; Cuban bread, cakes and Sicilian pastries.

places.name: Mauricio Faedo's Bakery
places.note: Old-line neighbourhood bakery with hot bread, pastelitos and a devoted following.

food.name: Cafe con leche
food.desc: Dark espresso cut with scalded milk and sugar, sipped with buttered Cuban toast - Tampa's morning ritual since the cigar era.

places.name: Naviera Coffee Mills
places.note: Roasting Tampa's coffee since 1921; the source of the beans behind most local cafe con leche.

places.name: La Segunda Bakery & Cafe
places.note: Coffee and buttered Cuban toast at the counter, exactly as Tampa has done it for a century.

places.name: Buddy Brew Coffee
places.note: Tampa's leading specialty roaster for those who want a modern take on the cortadito.

food.name: Tampa Bay craft beer
food.desc: Tampa helped define the American IPA and the pastry stout; taprooms cluster in Ybor, Seminole Heights and the warehouse district.

places.name: Cigar City Brewing
places.note: The brewery that put Tampa on the beer map with Jai Alai IPA; big tasting room and tours.

places.name: Coppertail Brewing Co.
places.note: Cavernous warehouse taproom on the edge of Ybor with a kitchen and rotating taps.

places.name: Angry Chair Brewing
places.note: Small-batch stouts with a cult national following; lines form for bottle releases.

landmarks: Henry B. Plant Museum (Tampa Bay Hotel)
This 1891 Moorish Revival palace with silver minarets was once a lavish resort and remains Tampa's most distinctive architectural icon.
Tampa Riverwalk
A scenic 2.6-mile waterfront path linking parks, museums, and skyline views along the Hillsborough River.
Sunshine Skyway Bridge
A soaring, cable-stayed bridge across Tampa Bay whose golden towers make it one of Florida's most photographed feats of engineering.
Ybor City Historic District
Tampa's atmospheric former cigar-making quarter, full of Cuban-Spanish brick architecture, wrought-iron balconies, and vibrant street life.
Tampa Theatre
A lavishly restored 1926 atmospheric movie palace with an ornate Mediterranean courtyard-style interior and glowing marquee.
Amalie Arena
The striking waterfront home of the Tampa Bay Lightning, a modern landmark on the downtown skyline and Riverwalk.
Curtis Hixon Waterfront Park
A lush green park on the Hillsborough River offering iconic postcard views of the downtown Tampa skyline.
Bayshore Boulevard
Home to the world's longest continuous sidewalk, this scenic waterfront drive frames unbeatable views of Tampa Bay and the skyline.
The Florida Aquarium
A dramatic glass-domed building on the Channelside waterfront showcasing Florida's rich marine and coastal ecosystems.
Busch Gardens Tampa Bay
An African-themed adventure park famed for its thrill rides and roaming wildlife, one of Tampa's most visited attractions.

train.note: No international trains serve Florida. Tampa Union Station at 601 N Nebraska Avenue, on the edge of downtown, sits at the end of a branch: Amtrak's Floridian (Chicago-Pittsburgh-Washington DC-Orlando-Miami) detours in from Lakeland and then reverses back out to Auburndale to continue south. The Silver Star was folded into the Floridian in November 2024, so check which name appears on your reservation. Amtrak Thruway coaches extend the network from Tampa to St Petersburg, Bradenton, Sarasota and Fort Myers, and southbound trains in particular can run hours behind the timetable.

bus.note: No international coaches from Tampa. Greyhound (https://www.greyhound.com/) uses the terminal at 610 E Polk Street downtown, FlixBus (https://www.flixbus.com/) stops at 1401 N Marion Street and runs the Orlando-Lakeland-Tampa-Sarasota-Fort Myers corridor, and RedCoach (https://www.redcoachusa.com/) runs more comfortable coaches north to Gainesville and Tallahassee and south to Miami from a stop near the USF campus. Orlando takes about 2 hours and Miami 6-7. Buy online for the cheapest fares, as counters keep short hours.

intl.to: St. Petersburg (USA) - from the Tampa Convention Center dock downtown

ferry.note: The Cross-Bay Ferry crosses Tampa Bay between the Tampa Convention Center and the St Petersburg Pier in under an hour, running Wednesday to Sunday during its season with adult fares around $10 - check the current schedule, because the service is grant-funded and its operating months shift from year to year. Tampa's cruise terminals on the Ybor Channel handle round-trip Caribbean and Mexico sailings from five lines rather than point-to-point transport. There are no international passenger ferries.
